findings.evidence: The pane files resolve as real paths in sibling probes (src/cli/panes/DaemonPane.tsx:53, src/cli/panes/ReposPane.tsx:62) and the earlier module.profile listed DaemonPane/ReposPane/WorkflowsPane/SetupPane/ModelTiersPane under src/cli/panes. The literal-filename grep returned 0 only because ripgrep scans contents, not names — the inventory holds.

findings.premise: The daemon exposes a `daemon.status` IPC that the CLI daemon service consumes to infer running/stopped (getStatus throw = stopped), and the stop path sends a `daemon.shutdown` RPC rather than a process signal.
findings.evidence: daemon.status handler at src/daemon/index.ts:849, consumed by src/cli/services/daemon.ts:50 (rpc<DaemonStatus>('daemon.status')); daemon.shutdown at daemon/index.ts:1347 + daemon.ts:77; getStatus-throw-means-stopped shown at cli/__tests__/tui.test.ts:107; stopDaemon at command.ts:84 + DaemonPane.tsx:53. Confirmed — the status card + stopped-inference + shutdown-RPC premises hold.

findings.premise: The daemon entry point that a `ps` cmdline scan would match is out/daemon/index.js (the compiled daemon binary the installer/CLI spawns).
findings.evidence: The daemon entry is DEFINED at src/cli/services/daemon.ts:24 as DAEMON_ENTRY = join(__dirname, '../../daemon/index.js') — i.e. the resolved absolute path ends in 'daemon/index.js' (compiled: .../out/daemon/index.js under the install root). The spec's 'out/daemon/index.js' is approximately right; the ps cmdline scan should anchor on the resolved DAEMON_ENTRY, not a hard-coded 'out/daemon/index.js' literal.
findings.action: Design (LLD) should ground the ps cmdline pattern on src/cli/services/daemon.ts:24 DAEMON_ENTRY (suffix 'daemon/index.js') rather than a fixed 'out/' prefix — noted, not a spec blocker.

findings.premise: Exactly two physical log files exist under PATHS.logDir today — daemon.log (daemon mode) and agent.log (shared by CLI mode and MCP mode) — written via the shared logger, and they are rotated (pino-roll).
findings.evidence: src/shared/paths.ts:104-105 define daemonLog + agentLog under LOG_DIR; src/shared/logger.ts has three pino-roll transports (lines 66/101/130) for the daemon/cli/mcp modes, with cli+mcp both routing to agentLog (src/bin/insrc-mcp.ts:39 setLogMode('mcp')). Exactly two physical files, rotated, agent.log shared by CLI + MCP — confirmed.
findings.action: None — the two-file + rotation premise (the basis for collapsing to two log categories) holds.

findings.premise: MCP client registration/connection status is obtained by running each CLI's `mcp list` (the same mechanism mcp-register.ts uses to register the insrc MCP server).
findings.evidence: src/daemon/mcp-register.ts (registerMcpClients) drives `mcp list` (mcp-register.test.ts:38 isList = args[0]==='mcp' && args[1]==='list') and `mcp add` via argv arrays. The per-client registration/status mechanism the MCP section reuses exists and is confirmed.

findings.premise: There is no existing debug-status IPC that enumerates the daemon's connected socket clients (label/pid/connected-at) — the spec proposes it as a NEW daemon IPC surface.
findings.evidence: No matches for debug-status/debugStatus/debug.status or any connected-clients/clientList/socketClients enumeration anywhere in src/ — confirming the debug-status IPC (status fields + live IPC client list) is genuinely a NEW surface the spec introduces, as claimed.
findings.action: None — the 'new IPC' premise is correct; design must add both the tracking + the method.

body.intent: Add a Debug pane/tab to the insrc TUI (alongside the existing Daemon / Repos / Workflows / Setup panes), navigated via inner sub-tabs — Daemon | MCP | Logs, keypress-switched, one section rendered full-height at a time. (1) Daemon: a status card (running/stopped, pid, uptime, version, socket path, managed-repo count + index state) sourced from the existing `daemon.status` IPC, polled continuously ('stopped' inferred the same way the existing Daemon pane does — the status RPC throwing/timing out); below it an orphan scan that shells out to `ps`, matches node processes by cmdline pattern against the daemon entry (`out/daemon/index.js`), excludes the managed daemon's own PID (from its status), and runs once on pane entry plus on an explicit refresh keypress. The pane's ONLY actionable control anywhere is a MULTI-SELECT guarded kill: the user selects ONE OR MORE detected orphan/zombie processes (the UI only recommends which look stray; selection is always explicit) and kills the selected set behind a confirm prompt, sending SIGTERM then escalating to SIGKILL after a ~3s timeout per still-alive PID. POSIX-only; on non-POSIX platforms (Windows) the section renders a 'orphan scan not supported on this platform' message instead of the scan UI. (2) MCP (read-only): (a) per-client (claude, codex) registration+connection status via each CLI's `mcp list`, run once on pane entry plus on-demand refresh; (b) the daemon's live IPC clients attached to the socket (label/pid/connected-at per client), sourced from a NEW daemon debug-status IPC call the TUI polls continuously. (3) Logs: the default view lists two categories — 'Daemon logs' (daemon.log) and 'Agent logs' (agent.log, shared by workflow/agent runs and the MCP subprocess); selecting one opens a live tail scoped to that category, sourced by the CLI tailing the known log file directly via fs.watch (no daemon IPC), resolving the most-recent ROTATED segment and following across rotation, with a persistent one-line filter bar (level / module / free-text search) above the tail that the user edits inline via keypress-driven field focus while the tail streams.
body.scopeBoundary: The pane is read-only EXCEPT for the single guarded multi-select orphan-kill control. It does NOT restart the managed daemon (that already lives in the main Daemon tab), does NOT disconnect/kill IPC clients from the MCP section, and offers no remediation action beyond the orphan kill. The Logs section tails at most ONE category at a time and does not split 'Agent logs' into separate workflow-run vs MCP-subprocess categories (no separate on-disk files exist today — only daemon.log and the shared agent.log). The orphan scan/kill is POSIX-only (macOS/Linux) — Windows gets a graceful 'not supported' message, not a cross-platform scan/kill path. Log data is read straight from disk (no new log-streaming IPC); the only new daemon IPC surface is the debug-status call (status card fields + live IPC client list).
